chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) who said:
There is no problem with wearing the safflower-dyed (clothing).

key_terms.المعصفر: Clothing dyed with 'usfur (safflower/Carthamus tinctorius), producing yellow-orange color; the permissibility of such garments was a topic of jurisprudential debate
key_terms.لا بأس: Standard legal formula meaning 'there is no objection/prohibition' — indicates permissibility (ibaha)

ai.seo_question: Is wearing safflower-dyed or saffron-colored clothing permitted in Islam?
ai.summary: One of the two Imams — either al-Baqir or al-Sadiq (peace be upon them both) — issued a ruling permitting the wearing of mu'asfar (safflower/saffron-dyed) garments. This is a fiqh ruling on clothing permissibility. Safflower-dyed clothing was debated among early Muslim scholars; some Sunni traditions discouraged it for men, while the Imam's ruling here grants explicit permission, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential tradition of careful nuance in dress regulations.
